resources.string:
Dashwheel uses Android's accessibility service to put two apps side by side, to make the steering wheel buttons do what you set, like Back, and to type what you dictate on your phone into the selected field.

For this it sees which apps are open and where, the buttons you press and the field you type in. It reads nothing else on the screen. Nothing is stored, sent or shared: it all stays on this unit.

With the Companion's touchpad, it also taps and scrolls where your phone's pointer is on the screen, and only then.
Dashwheel reads notifications to show what is playing, the next turn and new messages on the dashboard. They stay on this unit.
Android blocks this for apps installed from a file. Open settings and tap Dashwheel once, then App info, ⋮, Allow restricted settings, and try again.
